items.question: guy at the shop wants to slather the hoist line in that thick black tar dope so it lasts longer, any problem with that come inspection time
items.gold_answer: Rope lubricants of a type that hinder inspection must not be used. A heavy coating that hides the rope's condition from the inspector is not allowed.

key_quote.text: Rope lubricants that are of the type that hinder inspection must not be used.

items.question: befor we cut the wire rope to length do we need to put seizings on it, one side or both sides, and how many
items.gold_answer: Yes. Before cutting a wire rope, seizings must be placed on each side of the cut point. The length and number of seizings must follow the wire rope manufacturer's instructions.

key_quote.text: Prior to cutting a wire rope, seizings must be placed on each side of the point to be cut.

items.question: We have two lattice boom crawlers doing general hoisting. One was built in 2005 and its anti-two-block system only sounds a warning. The other was built in 2013 and has the same warning-only system. Is that OK on both machines?
items.gold_answer: On the 2005 crane (built after Feb 28, 1992), a device that warns the operator in time to prevent two-blocking at all points where it could occur is acceptable. A lattice boom crane built after November 8, 2011 must have a device that automatically prevents damage and load failure, so a warning-only system is not enough on the 2013 crane.

key_quote.text: Lattice boom cranes and derricks manufactured after November 8, 2011 must be equipped with a device which automatically prevents damage and load failure

items.variant: general hoisting, not the dragline/clamshell exception

items.question: drum rotation indicator quit on our 2015 machine and i cant see the drum from the seat what do i do til its fixed and how long do we have
items.gold_answer: Equipment built after Nov 8, 2011 with a hoist drum not visible from the operator's station needs a hoist drum rotation indicator. Until it's fixed, mark the drum to show its rotation, and install mirrors or remote video cameras and displays if the operator needs them to see the mark. As a Category II aid it must be repaired within 30 calendar days. If parts were ordered within 7 days and haven't arrived in time, the repair is due within 7 days of receiving them.

key_quote.text: Mark the drum to indicate the rotation of the drum.

items.question: The foot pedal brake lock on our crane is busted. Is that lock actually required? And can we work around it with some other measure until it's fixed, like the workarounds allowed for operational aids?
items.gold_answer: Yes. Equipment with foot pedal brakes must have locks, and the lock is a listed safety device. Operations must not begin unless it works properly. The equipment must be taken out of service until it is fixed, and alternative measures are not permitted.

key_quote.text: Alternative measures are not permitted to be used.

items.question: On the shift check I counted 7 random broken wires in one lay on the main hoist line. The rope maker has a written removal criterion for this exact rope that allows more broken wires than OSHA's number. Can we keep running it?
items.gold_answer: Six randomly distributed broken wires in one lay of a running rope is a Category II deficiency, so the rope can't be used until one of three things happens. The employer can follow the rope manufacturer's established removal criterion, or a different criterion the manufacturer approved in writing for that specific rope. Otherwise the rope must be replaced, or the damaged section cut out if the damage is localized (no splicing, at least 2 drum wraps left).

key_quote.text: The employer complies with the wire rope manufacturer's established criterion for removal from service or a different criterion that the wire rope manufacturer has approved in writing for that specific wire rope

items.expert_review_why: Whether a manufacturer's more lenient criterion allows continued use turns on how the criterion is read and documented.

items.question: found a whole strand popped on the whip line, is that rope junk or can we chop it, and do we gotta lock out the whole rig or just that drum
items.gold_answer: A broken strand is a Category III deficiency. The rope must be replaced, or if the damage is localized it can be cut in two and the undamaged part used (no splicing, at least two wraps left on the drum at the lowest position). Until then, either the whole equipment or the hoist with that rope must be tagged out.

key_quote.text: either the equipment (as a whole) or the hoist with that wire rope must be tagged-out

items.question: our boom truck is rated 5000 lbs built 2008, does it legaly have to have a load moment indicater or load weighing thing
items.gold_answer: No. The requirement for a load weighing device, load moment indicator or limiter applies only to equipment (other than derricks and articulating cranes) built after March 29, 2003 with a rated capacity over 6,000 pounds. A 5,000 lb rated machine is below that threshold.

key_quote.text: manufactured after March 29, 2003 with a rated capacity over 6,000 pounds must have at least one of the following

items.question: knuckle boom with a winch, built 2016, A2B is out. we can two-block it just by extending the boom without touching the winch. whats the fix til parts come
items.gold_answer: On an articulating crane built after Dec 31, 1999 with a load hoist, when two-blocking can happen without moving the load hoist, you must do both: mark the cable where the operator can easily see it, at a point that gives enough time to stop the hoist, and use a spotter when extending the boom. A2B is a Category I aid and must be repaired within 7 calendar days, or within 7 days of receiving parts that were ordered within 7 days.

key_quote.text: clearly mark the cable (so that it can easily be seen by the operator) at a point that will give the operator sufficient time to stop the hoist to prevent two-blocking, and use a spotter when extending the boom

items.variant: built after Dec 31, 1999, equipped with load hoist

items.question: Beyond what the shift inspection covers, what must the annual comprehensive wire rope inspection cover, and which areas of the rope need particular attention?
items.gold_answer: A qualified person must do a complete, thorough inspection of the surface of the entire length of the ropes for the Category I-III deficiency types. Particular attention goes to the critical review items, sections normally hidden during shift and monthly inspections, rope subject to reverse bends, and rope passing over sheaves.

key_quote.text: covering the surface of the entire length of the wire ropes
